inversion
law: to master a problem, study how to fail at it — then refuse to.
notes: instead of asking how to succeed, ask what would guarantee failure — then avoid it. many hard problems dissolve when worked backward.

name: via negativa
law: the surest improvement is removing what's wrong, not adding what's clever.
notes: improvement by subtraction: strip the fragile, the false, and the unnecessary before adding anything clever. what you remove can't break.

name: gell-mann amnesia
law: you trust the report on every subject but the one you happen to know.
notes: you read a story about a subject you know deeply and catch every error. you turn the page to a subject you don't know — and trust it completely.
